# Prompts for the shepherd's subagents

Fill the `{placeholders}` from `gh pr view N --json title,headRefName,headRefOid,additions,deletions,files,author`.
Add a line to the round-1 prompt only for what the PR's diff makes relevant: a file that a
recent merge also changed, a new reference file, an old PR. Do not add a conclusion.

## Review, round 1

```
You review PR #{N} in acme/ai-wiki: "{title}", head branch `{ref}`, +{adds}/-{dels}. You are
one of several independent reviewers; a separate session applies fixes and merges. Your
verdict decides whether this PR merges without a human, so be exact and do not rubber-stamp.

Repo: {repo_path}, checked out at `main`.{context_line}

Hard limits, because the working tree is shared:
- Read only. Do not run git checkout/switch/stash/reset/commit/push or `gh pr checkout`, and do
  not edit any file.
- Do not post comments, reviews or labels on GitHub.
- Read the PR head with `gh pr diff {N}`, `python3 ../bin/wikiloop pr-lines {N}` and
  `git show origin/{ref}:<path>` (run `git fetch -q origin {ref}` first). Read the base with
  `git show origin/main:<path>`.

Method: load the skill `wiki-pr-review` (this repo's `.claude/skills/`) and follow its steps 1-5. Answer three
questions for every changed passage:
1. Necessary? Gate, already there (grep origin/main), state vs mechanism, vendor lesson.
2. Too complex? Placement, size, the language rules, a new file where one sentence would do,
   SKILL.md router shape.
3. False? Verify every changed claim against its source: code, PRs and issues via `gh`, and
   the other tools this session has. If a source is out of reach, write "unverified: <claim>
   - <what is missing>". Never invent a mechanism to rescue a sentence.
For CLOSES_MISSING, read the "PR files that open candidates name" lines for #{N} in
`python3 ../bin/wikiloop inbox`; do not stretch a candidate to fit.

Return only this block, at most 60 lines, English, no names of people in proposed text:

VERDICT: merge | fix | block | close
FIX_SIZE: none | small | large   (small = all fixes together change fewer lines than the PR
          adds and need no new research)
CLOSES_MISSING: #N, ... | none
FINDINGS:
- F1 | <file>:<line at PR head> | <defect, one line> | <evidence or reason, one line>
  OLD: <exact unique text at the PR head, verbatim>
  NEW: <exact replacement text, or DELETE>
BLOCKERS: <for block: what a human must verify or decide, one line each> | none
OUT_OF_SCOPE: <defects you saw outside this PR's change, one line each> | none
KEPT: <one line: what is sound and stays>

Use `merge` only when FINDINGS is empty (wording preferences are not findings). Use `fix` when
every finding has an exact OLD/NEW. Use `block` when a claim cannot be verified, the PR
contradicts a sourced wiki sentence, a fix needs the author's knowledge, or the PR adds a skill
or changes a `description` without a trigger-eval case. Use `close` when the PR as a whole fails
the gate or duplicates the wiki.
```

## Review, round 2

To the round-1 reviewer, if it still runs in this session, or to a fresh one with the round-1
prompt plus this paragraph and the last shepherd comment:

```
Round 2 for PR #{N}: the fixes for round {R} are pushed; check them read-only and return the
same block. They are a new commit on top ({new_sha}), not an amend; the PR lands as a squash
merge. Same hard limits as before. Run `git fetch -q origin {ref}`, then
`git diff {reviewed_sha} origin/{ref}` and `git diff origin/main...origin/{ref}`.
Check: (1) each finding is applied as it was meant; (2) nothing else changed, and a merge of
main, if any, resolved the conflict as the finding says; (3) any new defect that the fix
itself introduced. Reopen accepted wording only for new evidence or a concrete missed defect.
Return the same VERDICT block; `merge` if all is good.
```

## The review comment

The run posts the reviewer's block unchanged under this head, so a later session can apply it:

```
<!-- shepherd round={R} verdict={verdict} sha={reviewed_sha} -->
**Automated wiki review, round {R}: {verdict}**

{reviewer block}
```

A `needs-human` comment adds one `Decision needed:` line and the options, one line each. When
the run escalates on its own (too many rounds, red checks), the comment starts with
`<!-- shepherd round={R} verdict=escalate sha={head} -->`, so a later push starts again at round 1.

## Lander

```
Land the open, accepted `candidate` issues of acme/ai-wiki in at most 2
PRs. Do not merge them: a separate reviewer checks each PR, and the shepherd merges it.

Repo: {repo_path}, on `main` at origin/main. You have the working tree to yourself.

The issues: {land_lines}
Plus defects that PR reviewers found outside their PRs; verify each before you change it:
{out_of_scope_lines}

1. Load `acme-wiki:wiki-contribute` and follow it: gate, placement, size caps, entry
   format, language, then `python3 ../bin/wikiloop build` and `wikiloop lint`.
2. For each issue, read the body and the triage comment (`gh issue view N --comments`). Verify
   the fact against its source before you write it. Do not copy a claim you cannot verify. One
   fact, one place: correct the existing sentence instead of a second copy.
3. An issue that fails the gate on a closer look, or that you cannot verify: do not land it;
   report it with a one-line reason. Do not close or relabel it.
4. At most 2 branches from origin/main, grouped by skill:
   `wiki/land-{date}-<group>`.
5. Commit subject `wiki(<skill>[, <skill>]): <what was learned>`; a body only for the why.
   No amend, rebase or force-push.
6. `gh pr create`: the body says where each fact came from and has one `Closes #N` line for
   each issue it lands. English, no names of people.
7. `git checkout main` when you finish.

Report in at most 40 lines: each PR URL and head SHA, then one line for each issue and defect:
landed (file and section) or skipped (reason).
```
